_comment: Targets for scripts/quality-score.ts — the stopping condition the brief asked for. Four axes, no rollup: a weighted score lets a cheap run that delivered nothing cancel a good one. `targets` is what 'done' means; `measured` is the last observed baseline, rewritten by --write. An axis with fewer than minSamples observations reports n/a and is never counted as a pass.

_targetRationale.deliveredPct: A stage that declares an artifact and writes nothing is the failure that started this work (run of 2026-08-01: 7 green stages, 0 files). Near-100 is the only defensible target for 'did it do what it said'.
_targetRationale.lagP95Seconds: run-health.ts measured a 43s median and a 14m worst case of pure post-answer waiting. 10s is the budget already used by `run-health.ts --p95`; keeping the same number means the two tools cannot disagree.
_targetRationale.paidTokensPerRun: Set from the measured A/B control arm (83k paid tokens for a three-step file-reading task). 60k is a deliberate ratchet below that, not a number the current system already meets.
_targetRationale.autonomyPct: No approval has ever been raised on this install, so this axis has no baseline yet — 90 is a placeholder that must be re-set from real data before it means anything.
